# Book III, Proposition 25

*The complete circle of a given segment*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> Given a segment of a circle, to describe the complete circle of which it is a segment.

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/25.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.25, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC be the given segment of a circle;

thus it is required to describe the complete circle belonging to the segment ABC, that is, of which it is a segment.

For let AC be bisected at D, let DB be drawn from the point D at right angles to AC, and let AB be joined;

the angle ABD is then greater than, equal to, or less than the angle BAD.

First let it be greater;

and on the straight line BA, and at the point A on it, let the angle BAE be constructed equal to the angle ABD; let DB be drawn through to E, and let EC be joined.

Then, since the angle ABE is equal to the angle BAE,

the straight line EB is also equal to EA. [I. 6]

And, since AD is equal to DC,

and DE is common,

the two sides AD, DE are equal to the two sides CD, DE respectively;

and the angle ADE is equal to the angle CDE, for each is right;

therefore the base AE is equal to the base CE.

But AE was proved equal to BE;

therefore BE is also equal to CE;

therefore the three straight lines AE, EB, EC are equal to one another.

Therefore the circle drawn with centre E and distance one of the straight lines AE, EB, EC will also pass through the remaining points and will have been completed. [III. 9]

Therefore, given a segment of a circle, the complete circle has been described.

And it is manifest that the segment ABC is less than a semicircle, because the centre E happens to be outside it.

Similarly, even if the angle ABD be equal to the angle BAD,

AD being equal to each of the two BD, DC,

the three straight lines DA, DB, DC will be equal to one another,

D will be the centre of the completed circle,

and ABC will clearly be a semicircle.

But, if the angle ABD be less than the angle BAD,

and if we construct, on the straight line BA and at the point A on it, an angle equal to the angle ABD, the centre will fall on DB within the segment ABC, and the segment ABC will clearly be greater than a semicircle.

Therefore, given a segment of a circle, the complete circle has been described.

Q. E. F.

From [`Elements/BookIII/Prop25.lean`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop25.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out, except three passages the Lean does not carry out. The list below marks where a lemma does a step Euclid takes for granted and where the Lean stops; the `/- … -/` notes in the listing explain smaller adjustments.

**How the Lean follows the text**

- **Done by `Postulate5`.** "let DB be drawn through to E…" Euclid takes for granted that AE meets DB drawn through; Postulate 5 gives it, the angles BAE, ABD being less than two right angles, since ABD is acute (I.17).
- **Left in Euclid's words.** "And it is manifest that the segment ABC is less than a semicircle…" The statement says where the centre falls, here across AC from B, which is Euclid's reason; it does not compare the segment with a semicircle.
- **Left in Euclid's words.** "and ABC will clearly be a semicircle." The statement says that D is the centre; it does not say that the segment is then a semicircle.
- **Left in Euclid's words.** "But, if the angle ABD be less than the angle BAD…" The Lean carries the construction, and the statement says that the centre falls on DB, on B's side of AC; that the segment is greater than a semicircle is not stated.

```lean
/-- Given a segment of a circle, to describe the complete circle of which it is a segment. -/
theorem Prop25 {A C : Point} {ABC : Circle} (hABC : ∃ E : Point, Centre E ABC) (hA : OnCircle A ABC)
    (hC : OnCircle C ABC) :
    ∀ P : Point, ¬ Collinear A C P → ∃ B D E : Point, OnCircle B ABC ∧ SameSideOf B P A C ∧
      Between A D C ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D C‖ ∧ ∠ A D B = ∟ ∧ Centre E ABC ∧ Collinear D B E ∧
      (∠ B A D < ∠ A B D → OppositeSidesOf E B A C) ∧ (∠ A B D = ∠ B A D → E = D) ∧
      (∠ A B D < ∠ B A D → SameSideOf E B A C) := by
  -- Let ABC be the given segment of a circle;
  intro P hP
  have hAC : A ≠ C := (show Triangle A C P from hP).ne₁₂
  -- thus it is required to describe the complete circle belonging to the segment ABC, that is,
  -- of which it is a segment.
  -- For let AC be bisected at D, let DB be drawn from the point D at right angles to AC, and
  -- let AB be joined;
  obtain ⟨D, hADC, hAD⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hAC
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hC_L⟩ := Postulate1 A C hAC
  have hD_L : OnLine D L := on_line_of_between_ends hADC hA_L hC_L
  obtain ⟨X, hXP, hX⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hAC ⟨L, hA_L, hC_L, hD_L⟩ hP
  have hD_in : InsideCircle D ABC := Prop2 hABC hA hC D hADC
  have hX_L : ¬ OnLine X L := hXP.triangle.off_line hA_L hC_L
  have hDX : D ≠ X := fun e => hX_L (e ▸ hD_L)
  obtain ⟨N, hD_N, hX_N⟩ := Postulate1 D X hDX
  obtain ⟨Y, hY_N, hXDY, -⟩ := Postulate2 hX_N hD_N hDX.symm []
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hB_N, hBDY⟩ :=
    line_circle_beyond hD_in hD_N hY_N (ne_of_between (between_symm hXDY))
  have hBD : B ≠ D := fun e => inside_not_on hD_in (e ▸ hB)
  have hB_L : ¬ OnLine B L := fun hB_L =>
    hX_L ((line_unique hBD hB_N hD_N hB_L hD_L) ▸ hX_N)
  have hY_L : ¬ OnLine Y L := fun hY_L =>
    hX_L ((line_unique (ne_of_between (between_symm hXDY)) hY_N hD_N hY_L hD_L) ▸ hX_N)
  have hBX : SameSide B X L := same_side_of_opposite_sides
    ⟨hY_L, hB_L, fun h => pasch3 hBDY hD_L (same_side_symm h)⟩
    ⟨hY_L, hX_L, fun h => pasch3 hXDY hD_L (same_side_symm h)⟩
  have hBP : SameSideOf B P A C := (SameSideOf.of_line hAC hA_L hC_L hBX).trans hXP
  have hBray : OnRay B D X := OnRay.of_between_between (between_symm hXDY) (between_symm hBDY)
  have hAD' : A ≠ D := ne_of_between hADC
  have hCD' : C ≠ D := (ne_of_between (between_symm hADC))
  have hADB : ∠ A D B = ∟ := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right hBray hAD']
    exact hX A ⟨L, hA_L, hC_L, hA_L⟩ hAD'
  have hABD : Triangle A B D := (Triangle.of_line hA_L hD_L hAD' hB_L).acb
  have hAB : A ≠ B := hABD.ne₁₂
  have hBC : B ≠ C := fun e => hB_L (e ▸ hC_L)
  have hA_N : ¬ OnLine A N := fun hA_N => hB_L ((line_unique hAD' hA_N hD_N hA_L hD_L) ▸ hB_N)
  -- the angle ABD is then greater than, equal to, or less than the angle BAD.
  rcases lt_trichotomy (∠ B A D) (∠ A B D) with h | h | h
  -- First let it be greater;
  -- and on the straight line BA, and at the point A on it, let the angle BAE be constructed
  -- equal to the angle ABD; let DB be drawn through to E, and let EC be joined.
  · obtain ⟨G, F, hF, hGD, hGAF⟩ := BookI.Prop23 hAB hABD hABD
    have hGA : G ≠ A := hGD.triangle.ne₁₃.symm
    have hBAG : ∠ B A G = ∠ A B D :=
      (angle_onRay_left hF hGA).symm.trans ((angle_symm hF.2.1 hGA).trans hGAF)
    obtain ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
    obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hG_K⟩ := Postulate1 A G hGA.symm
    /- Postulate 5 makes AG and DB produced meet, for the angles GAB, ABD are less than two
       right angles, ABD being less than a right angle [I. 17]. -/
    have hABD_lt : ∠ A B D < ∟ := by
      have h17 := (BookI.Prop17 hABD).1
      rw [angle_symm hBD hAD', hADB] at h17
      exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_right h17
    obtain ⟨E, hE_K, hE_N, hEG⟩ := Postulate5 hG_K hA_K hA_M hB_M hB_N hD_N hAB
      (hGD.sameSide hA_M hB_M)
      (by rw [angle_symm hGA hAB.symm, hBAG]; exact Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self hABD_lt)
    have hEG' : SameSideOf E G A B := SameSideOf.of_line hAB hA_M hB_M hEG
    have hED' : SameSideOf E D A B := hEG'.trans hGD
    have hEA : E ≠ A := hEG'.triangle.ne₁₃.symm
    have hEB : E ≠ B := hEG'.triangle.ne₂₃.symm
    have hEray : OnRay E A G := OnRay.of_sameSideOf hEG' ⟨K, hA_K, hG_K, hE_K⟩ hEA
    have hBAE : ∠ B A E = ∠ A B D := (angle_onRay_right hEray hAB.symm).trans hBAG
    have hEray' : OnRay E B D := OnRay.of_sameSideOf hED'.swap ⟨N, hB_N, hD_N, hE_N⟩ hEB
    /- E is beyond D: were it D, or between B and D, the angle BAE would not be greater than
       BAD. -/
    have hED : E ≠ D := fun e => by rw [e] at hBAE; rw [hBAE] at h; exact lt_irrefl _ h
    have hBDE : Between B D E := by
      rcases between_cases hBD hED.symm hEB.symm hB_N hD_N hE_N with h' | h' | h'
      · exact h'
      · exact absurd (between_symm h') hEray'.2.2.2
      · have hlt := angle_lt_of_between (V := A) (Triangle.of_line hD_N hB_N hBD.symm hA_N)
          (between_symm h')
        rw [angle_symm hEA hAB.symm, angle_symm hAD'.symm hAB.symm, hBAE] at hlt
        exact absurd (lt_trans hlt h) (lt_irrefl _)
    -- Then, since the angle ABE is equal to the angle BAE,
    have hABE : ∠ A B E = ∠ B A E := by
      rw [angle_onRay_right hEray' hAB, hBAE]
    -- the straight line EB is also equal to EA. [I. 6]
    have hEBA : Triangle E B A := (Triangle.of_line hB_N hE_N hEB.symm hA_N).bac
    have hEB_EA : ‖E B‖ = ‖E A‖ := BookI.Prop6 hEBA (by
      rw [angle_symm hEB hAB, hABE, angle_symm hAB.symm hEA])
    -- And, since AD is equal to DC,
    have hDA_DC : ‖D A‖ = ‖D C‖ := (len_symm D A).trans hAD
    -- and DE is common,
    have hDE : ‖D E‖ = ‖D E‖ := rfl
    -- the two sides AD, DE are equal to the two sides CD, DE respectively;
    -- and the angle ADE is equal to the angle CDE, for each is right;
    have hADE : ∠ A D E = ∟ := by
      rw [← adjacent_eq_of_right hB_N hE_N hBDE hA_N (by rw [angle_symm hBD hAD']; exact hADB),
        angle_symm hBD hAD', hADB]
    have hE_L : ¬ OnLine E L := fun hE_L =>
      hB_L ((line_unique hED hE_N hD_N hE_L hD_L) ▸ hB_N)
    have hCDE : ∠ C D E = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm hCD' hED, ← adjacent_eq_of_right hA_L hC_L hADC hE_L hADE, hADE]
    -- therefore the base AE is equal to the base CE.
    have hAE : ‖A E‖ = ‖C E‖ :=
      (BookI.Prop4 (Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hAD'.symm hE_L)
        (Triangle.of_line hD_L hC_L hCD'.symm hE_L) hDA_DC hDE
        (hADE.trans hCDE.symm)).1
    -- But AE was proved equal to BE;
    have h1 : ‖E A‖ = ‖E B‖ := hEB_EA.symm
    -- therefore BE is also equal to CE;
    have h2 : ‖E B‖ = ‖E C‖ := by rw [hEB_EA, len_symm E A, hAE, len_symm C E]
    -- therefore the three straight lines AE, EB, EC are equal to one another.
    -- Therefore the circle drawn with centre E and distance one of the straight lines AE, EB, EC
    -- will also pass through the remaining points and will have been completed. [III. 9]
    have hE : Centre E ABC := Prop9 hABC hA hB hC hAB hBC hAC h1 h2
    -- Therefore, given a segment of a circle, the complete circle has been described.
    -- And it is manifest that the segment ABC is less than a semicircle, because the centre E
    -- happens to be outside it.
    have hEB_AC : OppositeSidesOf E B A C :=
      OppositeSidesOf.of_line hAC hA_L hC_L ⟨hE_L, hB_L, pasch3 (between_symm hBDE) hD_L⟩
    exact ⟨B, D, E, hB, hBP, hADC, hAD, hADB, hE, ⟨N, hD_N, hB_N, hE_N⟩, fun _ => hEB_AC,
      fun h' => absurd (h'.symm ▸ h) (lt_irrefl _),
      fun h' => absurd (lt_trans h h') (lt_irrefl _)⟩
  -- Similarly, even if the angle ABD be equal to the angle BAD,
  -- AD being equal to each of the two BD, DC,
  · have hDA_DB : ‖D A‖ = ‖D B‖ := BookI.Prop6 (Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hAD'.symm hB_L) (by
      rw [angle_symm hAD'.symm hAB.symm, h, angle_symm hAB hBD.symm])
    -- the three straight lines DA, DB, DC will be equal to one another,
    have hDB_DC : ‖D B‖ = ‖D C‖ := by rw [← hDA_DB, len_symm D A, hAD]
    -- D will be the centre of the completed circle,
    have hD : Centre D ABC := Prop9 hABC hA hB hC hAB hBC hAC hDA_DB hDB_DC
    -- and ABC will clearly be a semicircle.
    exact ⟨B, D, D, hB, hBP, hADC, hAD, hADB, hD, ⟨N, hD_N, hB_N, hD_N⟩,
      fun h' => absurd (h ▸ h') (lt_irrefl _), fun _ => rfl,
      fun h' => absurd (h ▸ h') (lt_irrefl _)⟩
  -- But, if the angle ABD be less than the angle BAD,
  -- and if we construct, on the straight line BA and at the point A on it, an angle equal to
  -- the angle ABD, the centre will fall on DB within the segment ABC, and the segment ABC will
  -- clearly be greater than a semicircle.
  · obtain ⟨G, F, hF, hGD, hGAF⟩ := BookI.Prop23 hAB hABD hABD
    have hGA : G ≠ A := hGD.triangle.ne₁₃.symm
    have hBAG : ∠ B A G = ∠ A B D :=
      (angle_onRay_left hF hGA).symm.trans ((angle_symm hF.2.1 hGA).trans hGAF)
    /- The straight line AG falls within the angle BAD, and crosses BD at E. -/
    have hGB : SameSideOf G B A D := BookI.Prop24.within hGD.symm (by rw [hBAG]; exact h)
    obtain ⟨E, hBED, hEray⟩ := crossbar hGD hGB
    have hBAE : ∠ B A E = ∠ A B D := (angle_onRay_right hEray hAB.symm).trans hBAG
    have hE_N : OnLine E N := on_line_of_between_ends hBED hB_N hD_N
    have hED : E ≠ D := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBED)).symm
    have hEB : E ≠ B := (ne_of_between hBED).symm
    have hEA : E ≠ A := fun e => hA_N (e ▸ hE_N)
    /- As in the first case, EB is equal to EA [I. 6]. -/
    have hABE : ∠ A B E = ∠ B A E := by
      rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBED) hAB, hBAE]
    have hEBA : Triangle E B A := (Triangle.of_line hB_N hE_N hEB.symm hA_N).bac
    have hEB_EA : ‖E B‖ = ‖E A‖ := BookI.Prop6 hEBA (by
      rw [angle_symm hEB hAB, hABE, angle_symm hAB.symm hEA])
    /- AE is equal to CE, for the angles at D are right [I. 4]. -/
    have hADE : ∠ A D E = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBED)) hAD']; exact hADB
    have hE_L : ¬ OnLine E L := fun hE_L =>
      hB_L ((line_unique hED hE_N hD_N hE_L hD_L) ▸ hB_N)
    have hCDE : ∠ C D E = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm hCD' hED, ← adjacent_eq_of_right hA_L hC_L hADC hE_L hADE, hADE]
    have hAE : ‖A E‖ = ‖C E‖ :=
      (BookI.Prop4 (Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hAD'.symm hE_L)
        (Triangle.of_line hD_L hC_L hCD'.symm hE_L) (by rw [len_symm D A, hAD]) rfl
        (hADE.trans hCDE.symm)).1
    /- So the three straight lines AE, EB, EC are equal, and E is the centre [III. 9]. -/
    have h1 : ‖E A‖ = ‖E B‖ := hEB_EA.symm
    have h2 : ‖E B‖ = ‖E C‖ := by rw [hEB_EA, len_symm E A, hAE, len_symm C E]
    have hE : Centre E ABC := Prop9 hABC hA hB hC hAB hBC hAC h1 h2
    /- E lies between B and D, on B's side of AC, within the segment. -/
    have hEB_AC : SameSideOf E B A C :=
      SameSideOf.of_line hAC hA_L hC_L (pasch2 (between_symm hBED) hD_L hE_L)
    -- Therefore, given a segment of a circle, the complete circle has been described.
    exact ⟨B, D, E, hB, hBP, hADC, hAD, hADB, hE, ⟨N, hD_N, hB_N, hE_N⟩,
      fun h' => absurd (lt_trans h h') (lt_irrefl _),
      fun h' => absurd (h' ▸ h) (lt_irrefl _), fun _ => hEB_AC⟩
  -- Q. E. F.
```

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L73) (used here): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L65): If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between A and C. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L69): If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between A and D. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L146): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L42) (used here): If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L34): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L176): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L170): Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point A inside the second, and a point B outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L94): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L29) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35), [`Triangle.ne₁₂`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L22), [`Triangle.ne₁₃`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L36) and 3 other lemmas): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L41): Let a point be taken between B and C. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L49): Let a point be taken on the other side of L from B. (Points 6)
- [`exists_point_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L45): Let a point be taken on the same side of L as B. (Points 5)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L37) (used here): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L82): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, heading out to a point C outside it, cuts the circle between B and C. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L88) (used here): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L30) (used here): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L159) (through [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of L crosses L. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L45) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L48) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35), [`OnRay.of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L32), [`Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop13.lean#L189) and 3 other lemmas): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L51) (through [`OnRay.of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L32)): If B is between A and C, then A is not between B and C. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L78) (through [`OnRay.of_between_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L86)): If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L91) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35), [`OnRay.of_sameSideOf`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L186), [`SameSideOf.triangle`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L59) and 1 other lemma): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L55) (through [`OnRay.of_between_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L86)): A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes through C. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L60) (used here): A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L110) (used here): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L113) (used here): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L118) (through [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L98) (through [`same_side_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L111)): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L84): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L88) (used here): If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side as A. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L95) (through [`SameSideOf.trans`](../../Elements/Figure/Sides.lean#L53) and [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L130) (through [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L130)): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A. If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L138) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35)): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L55) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35) and [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L62) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35), [`angle_onRay_left`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L40) and [`angle_onRay_right`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L47)): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L78): Cutting a triangle in two from a vertex adds up. (Diagram-area 2)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L34): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L22): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L38): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`on_line_of_area_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L74): A triangle with no area has its corners on one straight line. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L50) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35) and [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L48): **Superposition.** A hypothetical placement of a triangle on a given ray and side permits a restricted derivation of metric equalities about the figure already given. The derivation introduces no further objects, cites each geometric law it uses, and exports no symbol of the placement.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (through [`Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self`](../../Elements/Figure/Areas.lean#L43), [`Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop13.lean#L189) and [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45) (through [`Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self`](../../Elements/Figure/Areas.lean#L43) and [`Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Figure/Lengths.lean#L50)): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35) (used here): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (used here): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (through [`BookI.Prop24.within`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop24.lean#L35) and [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

**Where will the centre fall?** Given only a piece of a circle, Euclid finds its centre and completes it. III.1's way is not open: there the straight line at right angles is halved between two points of the circumference, and here DB meets the segment's circumference only at B. So Euclid constructs at A an angle equal to the angle ABD, and which of the angles ABD, BAD is the greater says where the centre falls: beyond AC, at D, or within the segment, as the segment is less than a semicircle, a semicircle, or greater.

**"Will also pass through the remaining points."** Heath explains why Euclid says it: "it is still desirable to state … that 'the circle drawn with centre E and distance one of the straight lines AE, EB, EC *will also pass through the remaining points of the segment*' [III. 9], in order to show that part of the circle described actually coincides with the given segment" (vol. 2, p. 56). Our Lean has no word for a segment: we say it with the circle ABC, the straight line AC in it, and a point to name the side. So our statement is handed the whole circle, not the segment alone, and Euclid's E is its centre by III.9.

**"Produce BD, if necessary."** Robert Simson takes the semicircle first and the other two cases together, telling us to "produce BD, if necessary", which Heath finds "a little shorter than Euclid's procedure" (vol. 2, p. 56). H. M. Taylor bisects AC at right angles and then AB, and his two straight lines cross at Euclid's E.

**Why must AE meet DB?** Euclid takes the meeting for granted, and we prove it. In the first case Postulate 5 is the reason: the angle ABD is less than a right angle (I.17), so the angles BAE, ABD together are less than two right angles. In the third case AE crosses BD between B and D. Even B needs a word: D is within the circle, so DB meets the circumference.

**The modern way.** With D at the origin, A = (−a, 0), C = (a, 0) and B = (0, b), for positive a and b, the centre is E = (0, (b² − a²)/2b) and the radius (a² + b²)/2b. So E lies beyond AC, at D, or on B's side as b is less than, equal to or greater than a: Euclid's three cases.

## Further reading

- For the civil engineer who finds the centre of a running track or a railway curve "if we know any part of its arc", from two chords and their perpendicular bisectors, as H. M. Taylor completes the segment, David Eugene Smith's [*The Teaching of Geometry*](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/37681) (1911, free online), ch. XV (p. 202) (also on [III.14](14.md)).
- For the coordinates of the modern way, H. S. M. Coxeter's [*Introduction to Geometry*](https://www.wiley-vch.de/de/fachgebiete/mathematik-und-statistik/introduction-to-geometry-978-0-471-50458-0) (1969), ch. 8, "Coordinates", in a classic by a great geometer, with short, lively chapters.
